findings.title: SDK contract tests use a relative path after cd into drivers/cogent
findings.message: Earlier in the script the shell does `cd drivers/cogent` and never returns to the repo root, which is why check-example.sh is called through `$VELLUM_REPO_ROOT`. The new line uses a relative path, so `examples/sdk-contract` resolves under `drivers/cogent` and does not exist. `cd` fails and the contract tests are never run. Depending on `set -e`, that either aborts check.sh with an error or skips the check silently.
findings.suggestion: Use an absolute path via `$VELLUM_REPO_ROOT` (or `cd "$VELLUM_REPO_ROOT"` first) so the contract tests run from the repo root.

findings.title: otool parsing misreports fat/universal binaries as having non-system dependencies
findings.message: The parser skips only the first line of `otool -L` output. For universal (fat) binaries, otool prints a header line per architecture, such as `path (architecture arm64):`. Those lines are treated as dependencies, so every universal binary is rejected as having non-system native dependencies. The validator explicitly accepts the fat magic `\xca\xfe\xba\xbe`, so this path is reachable. Also, `otool` being absent raises a raw FileNotFoundError.
findings.suggestion: Skip arch header lines, i.e. any line that is not indented (`not line.startswith(("\t"," "))`), and only parse indented dependency lines. Optionally de-duplicate across architectures and handle a missing `otool` with a clear error.

findings.title: os.link used for final publication fails on filesystems without hardlink support
findings.message: Publishing the archive with `os.link` requires hardlink support on the destination filesystem. On FAT/exFAT, some network or container mounts, or restricted environments it raises OSError (EPERM/ENOTSUP), even though packaging succeeded. The temp directory is then deleted and nothing is produced.
findings.suggestion: Catch OSError from `os.link` and fall back to an exclusive copy: open `output` with mode `'xb'` and `shutil.copyfileobj` from the artifact, removing the partial output on failure. This keeps the no-overwrite guarantee.

findings.title: Overbroad 'build' path exclusion silently drops source
findings.message: Any tracked file with a path component named `build` is silently dropped from the SDK, not only the generated `drivers/cogent/build` directory. A legitimate Go package or example directory named `build` would be omitted without any warning. Consumers would then get a broken SDK, and the manifest would show nothing missing.
findings.suggestion: Exclude only the specific generated path, for example `name.startswith("drivers/cogent/build/")`, and keep skipping `__pycache__` generally.
findings.evidence: if "build" in path.parts or "__pycache__" in path.parts:

findings.title: Public release includes unverified, untracked dependency tree
findings.message: The public release cleanliness gate and the 'source changed during packaging' check rely on `git status`. Everything under `drivers/cogent/build/{upstream,typesetting}` is generated and most likely git-ignored. That content is packaged without any provenance or hash check, so a stale or locally modified dependency tree can ship in a 'clean' public archive and the gates will not notice. The recheck that the source is unchanged also cannot see these files.
findings.suggestion: For public builds, record and verify the dependency tree against an expected manifest or hash (for example from go.sum or a pinned commit). Alternatively regenerate the tree in a temporary directory during packaging, and compare dependency file hashes before and after.

findings.title: Published archive inherits 0600 permissions from temp file
findings.message: The archive is written to a `NamedTemporaryFile`, which is created with mode 0600, and it is hard-linked into place, so the published artifact keeps those permissions. A release archive that is unreadable by group and others is unexpected for something meant to be distributed or consumed by other users or CI. Hard-linking also fails on filesystems that do not support it, and the failure surfaces as a raw OSError.
findings.suggestion: Call `os.chmod(pending, 0o644)` before linking, and catch `OSError` around `os.link` to produce a clear error message.
